entries.name: Kapok
entries.flowers: white-pink, at night, bat-pollinated
entries.fruit: woody pod with silky kapok fibre
entries.voxel_shape: massive buttressed emergent, flat sparse crown high above the canopy
entries.notes: The classic emergent: one kapok visible over the whole forest. Buttresses flare up to 9 m; model the flare at ground level.

entries.name: Para rubber tree
entries.flowers: small cream panicles
entries.voxel_shape: tall straight trunk, roundish open crown with trifoliate leaves
entries.notes: Wild South America; nearly all rubber now comes from SE Asian plantations. Bark is tapped with a spiral cut; latex coagulates white.

entries.name: Brazil nut tree
entries.flowers: cream panicles, pollinated almost exclusively by Euglossine bees
entries.voxel_shape: tall columnar emergent, small crown, enormous trunk
entries.notes: Cannot set fruit without the big orchid bees, and the pods only fall whole: one player-hit drops a visibly heavy pod. A full-grown tree feeds families for centuries.

entries.name: Cocoa tree
entries.flowers: tiny pink, straight on the trunk and old branches (cauliflorous), midge-pollinated
entries.fruit: ridged pod, yellow-red, 20-60 beans in sweet pulp
entries.voxel_shape: small understory tree with football-sized pods stuck to the trunk
entries.notes: Flowers grow from bare bark, not twigs - the signature look. Midges do the pollinating, which is why it is famously fussy to farm.

entries.name: Honduran mahogany
entries.flowers: small greenish panicles
entries.fruit: erect woody capsule, winged seeds spin down
entries.voxel_shape: tall straight bole, rounded dense crown, buttresses at base
entries.notes: The hardwood that emptied the forests; CITES Appendix II. One big old trunk is a building, one felled mahogany is illegal loot.

entries.name: Iroko
entries.flowers: tiny, on wind-pollinated catkins
entries.voxel_shape: broad-spreading isolated crown on a thick clear bole
entries.notes: The savanna-forest-edge giant of West and East African folklore; said to house spirits, and respected enough that it is rarely cut.

entries.name: Gabon ebony
entries.flowers: small cream, urn-shaped
entries.voxel_shape: medium tree, dark crown; the inside is worth more than the outside
entries.notes: Jet-black heartwood, fantastically dense and slow to grow; critically endangered by carving demand and poached in its last strongholds in Gabon and Congo.

entries.name: Okoumé
entries.flowers: small whitish
entries.voxel_shape: tall straight bole with characteristic flaking reddish bark
entries.notes: The plywood tree of the Congo basin - nearly every marine plywood sheet on Earth started as okoumé. Almost never seen outside Africa.

entries.name: African oil palm
entries.flowers: dense spikes, insect and wind pollinated
entries.fruit: tight red-orange bunches, oil-rich mesocarp and kernel
entries.voxel_shape: tied-trunk palm, arching pinnate fronds, bunched red fruit
entries.notes: Native to the Gulf of Guinea; the world's highest-yield oil crop. Plantations replace rainforest wholesale - in this world, one of the main deforestation drivers.

entries.name: Açaí palm
entries.flowers: small cream on branched inflorescences from below the crown
entries.fruit: small round dark-purple drupe in hanging bunches
entries.voxel_shape: slender multi-stemmed palm, thin divided fronds
entries.notes: Slender multi-trunked palm standing in stilts on river islands. The berries are mostly skin and seed; the pulp is scraped, never squeezed - hence the nutty smoothie.

entries.name: Raffia palm
entries.leaves: evergreen, leaves up to 25 m - the longest of any palm
entries.flowers: branching inflorescences, dies flowering (monocarpic)
entries.fruit: large red-brown scales, inflating airtight baskets
entries.voxel_shape: short massive trunk with enormous arching 25 m fronds
entries.notes: Flowers once then dies - a 20 m arching tower of leaves. The fibre stripped from young leaves is raffia: string, weaving and gift bows.

entries.name: Buriti palm
entries.flowers: yellow-green panicles
entries.voxel_shape: tall solitary palm, star-like fan crown over swamp water
entries.notes: The swamp palm of the Amazon headwaters; whole buritizais floating on black peat. Fruit is pulled down by climbing; too spiny to pick any other way.

entries.name: Teak
entries.leaves: deciduous, dry season bare, among the biggest tree leaves
entries.flowers: white, in tall showy corymbs
entries.fruit: round corky drupe, floats when ripe
entries.voxel_shape: tall straight bole, open crown of huge opposite leaves
entries.notes: Oily heartwood that laughs at salt water - the deck timber of every age-of-sail ship. Thrives on the monsoon's wet-dry rhythm; bare for months a year.

entries.name: Yellow meranti
entries.flowers: small greenish, massed every few years (mast fruiting)
entries.voxel_shape: impossibly tall column vanishing into the mist, buttressed base, tiny crown
entries.notes: The tallest tropical tree ever measured: 'Menara', 97.6 m in Sabah, 2019 (recently reclassified Richetia faguetiana). Logging bans protect the last giants; endangered.

entries.name: Strangler fig
entries.flowers: hidden inside the fig, fig-wasp pollinated
entries.fruit: small round figs, eaten by birds
entries.voxel_shape: broad green canopy with a cage of fused roots; the dead host rots away inside
entries.notes: Starts as an epiphyte on a branch and strangles its host to death by a thousand merged roots. The hollow 'fig trees' of coast and swamp are empty host chimneys.

entries.name: Indian rubber fig
entries.leaves: evergreen, big glossy leaves with red sheaths, milky latex
entries.flowers: inside the fig (fig wasp)
entries.voxel_shape: broad dense crown of giant waxy leaves; aerial roots hanging like curtains
entries.notes: The original india-rubber source, eclipsed by Hevea. Indoors it is the bullet-proof rubber plant; outdoors in the tropics it becomes a brooding giant.

entries.name: Coca
entries.flowers: tiny cream
entries.voxel_shape: bushy shrub with small oval leaves, unassuming in every way
entries.notes: Sacred to Andean peoples for millennia; the source of cocaine, so heavily trafficked its wild range is now mapped by satellite. Real, and never just a bush in this world.

entries.name: Balsa
entries.flowers: large cream-yellow trumpets, night-opening
entries.fruit: long 5-part capsule with floating fluffy seeds
entries.voxel_shape: flagpole trunk rocketing up, sparse light crown
entries.notes: The fastest-growing tree on Earth, up to a metre a year; wood density ~100-200 kg/m3, light enough to float. Barely rots for years, which is why natives built rafts from it.

entries.name: Guadua bamboo
entries.flowers: rarely - gregarious mass flowering every ~25-30 years, then the plant dies
entries.voxel_shape: dense thicket of 20 m jointed green canes, razor-thin nodes
entries.notes: A grass pretending to be a forest: culms to 25 cm, entire groves flowering and dying in the same decade. Bamboo forests are fire-prone tinder when dead.

entries.name: Silver tree fern
entries.leaves: evergreen, arching fronds to 4 m, silvery-black stalks with white scales
entries.voxel_shape: trunk of fibrous black bristles, umbrella crown of enormous fronds
entries.notes: New Zealand's silver fern made actual national flag material; its crown shades out the forest floor below. If a voxel biome needs a 'phase 2' canopy, this is it.

entries.name: Bird's-nest fern
entries.leaves: evergreen, strap-like fronds in a rosette like a hanging basket
entries.voxel_shape: green rosette sitting on branches, not soil - epiphyte on every tree
entries.notes: Grows on branches and rocks collecting leaf litter in its basket; a rainforest is not a rainforest until the canopy is wearing these.

entries.name: Dawson's giant moss
entries.leaves: evergreen, stiff prickly leaves in one rank
entries.voxel_shape: stiff upright green blades waving 50 cm high, like a miniature pine forest
entries.notes: The tallest self-supporting moss on Earth at 60 cm - with conducting cells analogous to true plants. In voxel scale it is half a block of storytelling.

entries.name: Hanging lobster-claw heliconia
entries.flowers: red bracts tipped yellow-green, hanging like lobster claws, hummingbird-pollinated
entries.voxel_shape: broad banana-leaf clumps with red hanging claw inflorescences
entries.notes: Hummingbird's favourite feeder; the red-yellow-green hanging claws are readable from any distance and sway differently from every other plant in the canopy storey.

entries.name: Ruby-lipped cattleya
entries.flowers: magenta-pink with crimson-veined lip, intensely fragrant
entries.voxel_shape: small cluster of swollen stems with two-toned magenta flowers
entries.notes: The original corsage orchid, native only to Brazil's Atlantic forest - looted nearly to extinction for flower shows. Grows on branches: another canopy-wearer.

entries.name: Vanilla
entries.flowers: greenish-white, ephemerous, pollinated by one bee in Mexico; hand-pollinated everywhere else
entries.fruit: the vanilla pod/bean; cured for months for flavour
entries.voxel_shape: scrambling succulent vine with thick pale leaves and dangling beans
entries.notes: A climbing orchid. Outside Mexico only hand-pollination works, which is why Madagascar outproduces the whole origin continent. Second-most valuable spice on Earth.

entries.name: Split-leaf philodendron
entries.leaves: evergreen, huge leaves that split/fenestrate as the plant matures
entries.flowers: cream spathe and spadix
entries.fruit: pineapple-flavoured green cone, edible when ripe (stinging unripe)
entries.voxel_shape: massive climbing vine of pierced leaves seeking the canopy
entries.notes: Deliciosa because the ripe fruit tastes of pineapple; unripe fruit is full of irritating calcium oxalate needles. The monster of every plant-fluencer's feed, growing up trees.

entries.name: Rattan
entries.leaves: evergreen, pinnate with thorny climbing whips
entries.flowers: branched inflorescences armed with recurved claws
entries.voxel_shape: slender thorny canes draped between trees, crown-top palm flowers
entries.notes: A climbing palm whose thin stems reach 50-100 m - the longest plants on Earth. Every wicker chair and rattan sofa grows off a rainforest tree trunk at 10 m up.

entries.name: Rajah Brooke's pitcher plant
entries.leaves: evergreen, leaves ending in 35 cm pitchers holding up to 3.5 L of digestive fluid
entries.flowers: small reddish on a climbing stem
entries.voxel_shape: scrambling vine with enormous dark-green helmet pitchers
entries.notes: Endemic to Mt Kinabalu and Mt Tambuyukon, just two ridges of Borneo. Its pitchers are frog pits and rat traps with a roof; well-kept individuals are dolled up as garden trophies.

entries.name: Amazon water lily
entries.leaves: floating pads up to 3 m across, ribbed with 10 cm upturned rims, spiny beneath
entries.flowers: white opening the first night, pink the second; beetle-pollinated, pineapple-scented
entries.voxel_shape: giant floating lily-pad disc with a raised pink-to-white rim
entries.notes: Pads 3 m wide, 7-8 m petioles, carrying 40+ kg dry - a child could stand on one. National flower of Guyana; the inspiration for the 1851 Crystal Palace design.

entries.name: Water hyacinth
entries.flowers: lilac spike with a yellow-eyed petal
entries.voxel_shape: dense mat of round leaves and lilac spikes carpeting a still pool
entries.notes: Native to the Amazon; the fastest-spreading aquatic weed on Earth. Introduced as an ornament in 1884 and now chokes rivers on every continent - doubling every two weeks.

entries.name: Titan arum
entries.leaves: one single 6 m compound leaf instead of a stem, huge fan
entries.flowers: burgundy-and-green spathe around a 2-3 m golden spadix; stinks of rotting meat, blooms a day every 7-10 years
entries.voxel_shape: the world's largest unbranched inflorescence towering 3 m above a frilly skirt
entries.notes: 'Corpse flower' with a 50 kg tuber. When it blooms, crowds line up outside botanic gardens; native only to a few Sumatran gorges and pollinated by carrion beetles and flies.

entries.name: Rafflesia
entries.flowers: largest single flower on Earth, ~1 m across, 11 kg, five mottled rust-red lobes, carrion smell, lasts 5-7 days
entries.fruit: dark berry with minute seeds (trapped in rotting carcasses modelled by researchers)
entries.voxel_shape: a mottled meat-coloured dinner plate flower lying on the forest floor
entries.notes: No leaves, stems or roots: a body of threads inside a Tetrastigma vine until it bursts out as the world's biggest flower. Entire plant is the bloom; help it and you win.

entries.name: Zombie-ant fungus
entries.voxel_shape: a small orange club erupting from a frozen ant locked to a leaf's underside
entries.notes: Hijacks an ant, marches it uphill, locks its jaws on the leaf vein at noon, and fruiting bodies burst from the skull. One of the only organisms named in a horror label.

entries.name: Starfish fungus
entries.voxel_shape: a 15 cm red starfish lying on the mulch, glistening with brown goo
entries.notes: Red arms around a foul tip of olive slime attracting flies to carry its spores; first formally described in 1792. Looks like an alien washed up after the rain.

entries.name: Green pepe
entries.voxel_shape: tiny fan caps glowing faint green on dead wood after dusk
uses: none (glows for about three nights per flush)
entries.notes: Bioluminescent caps emitting a ghostly green light for a few nights after rain; a cluster of these under a buttress is free nighttime voxel lighting.

entries.name: Old man's long beard
entries.voxel_shape: 3-8 m hanging grey-green threads from branch tips
entries.notes: Epiphyte so sensitive to sulphur dioxide that its presence certifies clean air; the first thing air pollution kills. A bare cloudforest branch wearing a metre of grey beard.
